papers.title: EXPERT: A practical and forward-looking guide to capturing protein expression and purification metadata to develop machine learning models.
papers.abstract: As machine learning (ML) becomes increasingly important in protein engineering, synthetic biology, and bioprocess optimization, the lack of consistent, complete, and standardized experimental reporting remains a major barrier to building effective models. EXPERT (EXpression and Purification Experimental Reporting Template) defines a structured framework for capturing protein expression and purification data across the community, to increase reproducibility across laboratories and support downstream ML applications. We propose here the essential data that should be recorded during expression an
papers.summary: EXPERT proposes a standardized template for recording protein expression and purification metadata, addressing the lack of consistent experimental reporting that hinders machine learning model development. The framework aims to improve reproducibility across labs and enable the aggregation of high-quality datasets for training ML models in protein engineering and bioprocess optimization.

papers.title: Lessons From CABBI: Advancing Vegetative Oil Production in C4 Crops Through a Vertically Integrated DBTL Framework.
papers.abstract: The global demand for renewable liquid fuels and biobased chemicals has intensified interest in engineering high-biomass C4 grasses to accumulate triacylglycerol (TAG) in vegetative tissues. Achieving this goal requires coordinated solutions across molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment, disciplines that rarely operate within a single research program. The Center for Advanced Bioenergy and Bioproducts Innovation (CABBI) was established to provide this integration through a Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) framework applied to three C4 feedstocks: sacchar
papers.summary: This perspective describes how the CABBI center organized a vertically integrated Design-Build-Test-Learn pipeline to engineer C4 grasses (such as sorghum, sugarcane, and miscanthus) to accumulate triacylglycerol (vegetative oil) in their biomass for renewable fuels and biobased chemicals. It argues that progress on this goal requires coordinating molecular biology, crop science, chemical engineering, and life cycle assessment within a single program rather than in isolated labs. The paper distills lessons from CABBI's cross-disciplinary structure as a model for bioenergy crop engineering.

papers.title: Early Prediction and Prognosis in Acute Kidney Injury Using a Biomarker-Aware Transformer: Retrospective Multicenter Study.
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common, life-threatening complication among hospitalized patients. Timely prediction is crucial for prevention, while accurate prognosis following onset is essential for guiding care. Although electronic health records (EHRs) provide rich longitudinal data, their high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity pose challenges for traditional machine learning.
papers.summary: This retrospective multicenter study develops a biomarker-aware Transformer model that leverages longitudinal electronic health record data to both predict the onset of acute kidney injury (AKI) in hospitalized patients and forecast prognosis after onset. The approach addresses the high dimensionality, heterogeneity, and temporal complexity of EHR data that challenge conventional machine learning methods, aiming to support earlier prevention and better post-onset care decisions.

papers.title: scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell spatial omics (SCSO) has reshaped spatial profiling by enabling simultaneous molecular characterization and spatial mapping at single-cell resolution, providing insights into cellular identities and tissue architecture within native biological contexts. By integrating spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities, SCSO datasets have been widely used to construct spatially resolved cell atlases, characterize disease-associated tissue remodeling, and map disease-relevant cell populations. However, these SCSO datasets remain fragmented across individual publications,
papers.summary: scSpatial is a new atlas/database that consolidates single-cell spatial omics datasets, which were previously scattered across individual publications. It integrates spatial coordinates with molecular profiles and cell identities to support construction of spatially resolved cell atlases and characterization of disease-associated tissue remodeling. The resource aims to make SCSO data more accessible and reusable for the spatial omics community.

papers.title: Precision Nutrition and Health Outcomes Across the Lifespan.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition is an emerging paradigm that seeks to tailor dietary recommendations and interventions based on individual and population characteristics. Although advances in multi-omics, wearable sensors, and artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) have accelerated discovery, translation into practice remains limited by fragmented evidence across life stages and insufficient integration of knowledge regarding systems biology and other influences on health. Nutritional needs, vulnerabilities, intervention opportunities, and response heterogeneity evolve dynamically from preconcep
papers.summary: This review argues that precision nutrition—tailoring dietary advice using multi-omics, wearables, and AI/ML—has advanced rapidly in discovery but lags in clinical translation because evidence is fragmented across life stages and poorly integrated with systems biology. The authors call for a lifespan-spanning framework that accounts for how nutritional needs and response heterogeneity change from preconception onward.

papers.title: Ontology- and Data-Driven Circularity Assessment of Waste-Derived Rigid PVC-u: A Micro-Macro Decision Framework for Sustainable Recycling and Smart Manufacturing.
papers.abstract: The circularity of waste-derived rigid unplasticised poly (vinyl chloride) (PVC-u) is constrained by heterogeneous waste-stream sources, degraded material quality, legacy additives, and inconsistent decision criteria spanning technical, environmental, and economic aspects. In this work, we developed an ontology- and data-driven circularity assessment framework for waste-derived rigid PVC-u recycling systems, built on a Protégé ontology coupled with big data analytics. The framework structures knowledge on materials, recycling processes, process parameters, quality aspects, sustainability measu
papers.summary: The authors developed a framework for assessing how circular waste-derived rigid PVC recycling can be, combining a Protégé ontology with big data analytics to organize knowledge about materials, processes, quality, and sustainability criteria. It aims to support decision-making across technical, environmental, and economic dimensions for sustainable recycling and smart manufacturing.

papers.title: WingShape-Warn: A Morphology-Driven Early-Warning Pipeline for Mosquito-Borne Disease Surveillance.
papers.abstract: Environmental stressors-including climate change, urbanisation, and pollution-are increasingly altering the wing morphology of mosquito vectors. These morphological shifts, particularly in wing geometry, can serve as early-warning indicators for mosquito abundance and arboviral disease outbreaks. However, quantitative wing-shape analysis remains underutilised in operational mosquito surveillance and public health early-warning systems. This Technology and Code article presents WingShape-Warn, a reproducible, open-source pipeline that integrates geometric morphometrics, deep learning-based imag
papers.summary: WingShape-Warn is an open-source, reproducible pipeline that combines geometric morphometrics with deep learning-based image analysis to quantify mosquito wing shape from images. The authors propose that wing morphology shifts driven by environmental stressors can act as early-warning indicators of mosquito abundance and arboviral outbreak risk, aiming to bring quantitative wing-shape analysis into operational surveillance. The work is a technology/code contribution rather than a validated field study.

papers.title: Comparative Genomic Analysis Reveals Evolutionary Features of Glugea plecoglossi, a Fish-Infecting Microsporidian Parasite of Ayu (Plecoglossus altivelis).
papers.abstract: Microsporidia are obligate intracellular parasites with extensively reduced genomes, yet substantial genomic variation occurs among lineages. Glugea plecoglossi infects ayu (Plecoglossus altivelis) and forms conspicuous xenomas, but its genome characteristics and evolutionary position remain poorly resolved. We generated a genome assembly of G. plecoglossi and compared it with 42 additional microsporidian taxa using phylogenomics, functional profiling, repeat analysis, and multi-copy orthogroup analysis. The 16.71 Mb assembly comprised 59 scaffolds, with a scaffold N50 of 557.5 kb and 78.5% co
papers.summary: This study presents a genome assembly of Glugea plecoglossi, a microsporidian parasite that infects ayu fish and forms xenomas, and compares it with 42 other microsporidian taxa. The 16.71 Mb assembly reveals evolutionary features of this lineage and provides a phylogenomic framework for understanding genome variation among these reduced-genome intracellular parasites.

papers.title: An Ontology for Workplace Violence: Protocol to Support Cross-Sector Incident Reporting in Public Services.
papers.abstract: Underreporting is a defining problem in the documentation of workplace violence across public services. This is reinforced by inconsistent, often poor incident descriptions and the absence of a clear, shared nomenclature. Without an ontology-backed structure, similar events are recorded differently across settings or remain uncodable and effectively invisible. Moreover, workplace violence (WPV) is typically registered and studied within sector- and even organization-specific categories and local reporting logics rather than through a shared semantic framework, limiting comparability and cumula
papers.summary: This protocol paper proposes developing a shared ontology for workplace violence (WPV) incident reporting across public services, addressing the problem of inconsistent terminology and underreporting that makes events hard to compare or even record. The authors argue that sector-specific reporting logics prevent cumulative analysis, and an ontology-backed semantic framework would enable cross-sector comparability. The work is at the protocol stage, describing the planned approach rather than presenting a completed ontology or validation results.

papers.title: Applications and Future Prospects of Plant Multi-Omics Technologies in Precision Agriculture.
papers.abstract: Against the backdrop of global population growth, intensifying climate change, and limited arable land, ensuring food security and promoting sustainable agriculture have become critical issues. The limitations of conventional agricultural systems are becoming increasingly apparent, creating an urgent need for innovation driven by science and technology. In this context, plant multi-omics technologies serve as the foundational data and technical cornerstone of systems biology and precision agriculture. Integrating multi-level data from genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigen
papers.summary: This review surveys how integrating plant genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics can support precision agriculture under pressures from population growth, climate change, and limited arable land. It argues that multi-omics data form the foundational layer for systems-biology-driven crop improvement and outlines applications and future prospects. The piece is a broad overview rather than a primary research contribution.

papers.title: Endogenous APP-Associated Proteomics in Mouse Brain Defines a Candidate Resource for APP Trafficking and Proteostasis Studies.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Affinity proteomics of amyloid precursor protein (APP) is complicated by proteolytic processing, dynamic trafficking, and purification background. We generated a C-terminal 3×FLAG knock-in at the endogenous App locus to establish a cortical affinity-proteomic resource and prioritize APP-associated candidates for further study. Methods: Eight-week-old male homozygous APP-3×FLAG mice on a C57BL/6J background and wild-type littermates were characterized by biochemical and behavioral assays (n = 6 and n = 7 per genotype, respectively). Cortical material from three APP-3×FLAG
papers.summary: The authors created a 3×FLAG knock-in at the endogenous App locus in mice to enable affinity purification of APP and its associated proteins from cortical tissue, addressing challenges from APP's proteolytic processing and dynamic trafficking. They characterized the mice biochemically and behaviorally and generated a candidate list of APP-associated proteins for future trafficking and proteostasis studies. This provides a reusable resource for the APP research community.

papers.title: EBV-HSA-RegDB: A database of regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus and human miRNAs.
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a ubiquitous human herpesvirus associated with various malignancies and autoimmune diseases. MiRNAs play crucial roles in viral-host interactions by regulating gene expression post-transcriptionally. Understanding the regulatory networks between EBV-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs is essential for elucidating viral pathogenesis and identifying therapeutic targets. We reported the EBV-HSA miRNA Regulatory Database (EBV-HSA-RegDB, https://lbcd.ufpa.br/ebvhsa or  https://lbcd.ia.br/ebvhsa ), an integrated bioinformatics resource that combines comparative sequence analy
papers.summary: This paper presents EBV-HSA-RegDB, a curated bioinformatics database cataloging regulatory interactions between Epstein-Barr virus-encoded miRNAs and human miRNAs. The resource integrates comparative sequence analysis to map viral-host miRNA regulatory networks, aiming to support research on EBV pathogenesis and therapeutic target discovery. It is a specialized, web-accessible resource for researchers studying EBV-host interactions.

papers.title: Comparative Toxicity of Antifouling Paint Particle Suspensions and Dissolved Leachates in the Marine Copepod Tigriopus japonicus.
papers.abstract: Antifouling paint particles (APPs), generated by coating degradation and ship-maintenance activities, are an emerging but poorly characterized source of marine pollution. APPs can release particle-associated and dissolved toxicants, yet their relative contributions to toxicity remain unclear. In this study, environmentally collected APPs were used to prepare two exposure media: an APP suspension containing suspended paint particles and dissolved constituents, and a corresponding membrane-filtered leachate representing the operationally defined dissolved fraction. Their toxic effects on the mar
papers.summary: This study compared the toxicity of suspended antifouling paint particles versus the dissolved leachate from the same particles in the marine copepod Tigriopus japonicus. The authors found that the two exposure media produced differing toxic effects, helping clarify the relative contributions of particle-associated versus dissolved toxicants from this emerging marine pollutant. The work highlights that antifouling paint particles are a distinct and underappreciated source of marine contamination.

papers.title: Unlocking the full potential of spatial omics in plants: practical challenges, solutions, and a path forward.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics technologies provide new opportunities for plant biology by enabling molecular profiling within structurally intact tissues, revealing spatially organized cell states, developmental gradients, and regulatory interactions. While spatial transcriptomics has driven early advances, the field is rapidly expanding toward integrated spatial multi-omics by combining single-cell and spatial transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data. These approaches offer new opportunities to study development, physiology, and plant biotic and abiotic interactions in spatially preserved
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial omics technologies can be applied to plant biology, moving beyond spatial transcriptomics toward integrated multi-omics approaches that combine transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data within intact tissue contexts. It outlines practical challenges specific to plant tissues and proposes solutions and a roadmap for broader adoption.

papers.title: PanRes: a database of latent and acquired antimicrobial resistance allowing 3D-based protein homology search.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance databases are central to genomic surveillance, but resistance determinants remain distributed across resources with different scopes, structures, and annotations.
papers.summary: PanRes is a new database that consolidates antimicrobial resistance determinants from multiple sources into a single resource, addressing the fragmentation of resistance data across different databases. It also introduces a 3D-based protein homology search, allowing users to find resistance proteins by structural similarity rather than just sequence. This could improve the detection of novel resistance genes that share structural features with known ones.

papers.title: Dermatopathology 2030: Navigating the Digital, Computational and Molecular Convergence for Precision Diagnostics-Originated from a Round Table Discussion at A 66, Basel.
papers.abstract: Background: Traditional dermatopathology relies on analog, qualitative pattern recognition, which encounters critical limitations when facing diagnostic "gray zones" and ambiguous tumor proliferations. Objectives: This paper synthesizes a comprehensive framework integrating Whole Slide Imaging (WSI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and multi-omics to evaluate how this structural convergence redesigns diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems toward 2030. Methods: We analyze the conceptual shift from individual microscope-based observation to multiple data integration. We integrate recent algorithmic
papers.summary: This perspective piece, based on a round table at the 66th Basel dermatopathology meeting, argues that dermatopathology is shifting from analog microscope-based pattern recognition toward an integrated digital ecosystem combining whole-slide imaging, artificial intelligence, and multi-omics. The authors propose a framework for how this convergence could improve diagnosis of ambiguous tumors and diagnostic gray zones by 2030, while also reshaping risk and safety considerations.

papers.title: MTB-KB: A Curated Knowledgebase of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Related Studies.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), has regained its position as the world's leading killer among infectious diseases. Despite extensive research progress across epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, treatment regimens, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence factors, and immune mechanisms, MTB-related knowledge remains fragmented across thousands of publications, limiting its application in research and clinical practice. To address this gap, we present MTB-KB, a literature-curated knowledgebase that systematically integrates high-impact findings from eight major
papers.summary: MTB-KB is a literature-curated knowledgebase that systematically integrates high-impact findings on Mycobacterium tuberculosis from eight major research areas, including epidemiology, diagnosis, drug development, treatment, vaccines, drug resistance, virulence factors, and immune mechanisms. It addresses the fragmentation of TB knowledge across thousands of publications, aiming to make this information more accessible for research and clinical applications.

papers.title: DHX15 as a novel immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer: An integrated bioinformatics analysis with in vitro functional validation.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is a disease that occurs relatively frequently, and its prognosis and treatment outcomes are not optimal at present. Identifying novel BC biomarkers and therapeutic targets is key. DEAH-box helicase 15 (DHX15) is an RNA helicase that exhibits enhanced activity and is closely associated with tumorigenic potential. Alternative splicing is widely dysregulated in BC. However, the biological function of DHX15 in BC, in addition to its underlying molecular mechanisms, remain unclear. DHX15, a key RNA helicase involved in splicing regulation, was therefore selected to explore wheth
papers.summary: This study identifies the RNA helicase DHX15 as a potential immune-related prognostic biomarker in breast cancer using integrated bioinformatics analysis, supported by in vitro functional validation. The authors link DHX15 expression to alternative splicing dysregulation and tumorigenic potential, suggesting it may serve as both a prognostic indicator and therapeutic target.

papers.title: Methods for determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions to facilitate antimicrobial stewardship: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Effective antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) requires accurate information on the reason for prescribing antimicrobials. To design targeted interventions aimed at improving guideline adherence, accurate information on the indication for each prescription is necessary. This scoping review maps the existing methods used for systematically determining indications for antibiotic prescriptions.
papers.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
papers.summary: This scoping review maps methods for systematically determining the indication for antibiotic prescriptions, a prerequisite for effective antimicrobial stewardship. It catalogs existing approaches to capture prescribing rationale, which can inform targeted interventions to improve guideline adherence.

papers.title: Modeling Strategies for Neurodegenerative Diseases: In Vitro, In Vivo and In Silico Frameworks.
papers.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by complex etiologies, multifactorial pathogenic mechanisms, and remarkable clinical and molecular variability. Their increasing prevalence poses an important challenge to healthcare systems, society and the global economy. Despite decades of research, effective disease-modifying therapies remain elusive, highlighting the urgent need for reliable disease models capable of unraveling pathogenic mechanisms and supporting the development of personalized therapeutic strategies. Modeling NDs remains inherentl
papers.summary: This review surveys the current landscape of neurodegenerative disease models across three complementary frameworks: in vitro systems (cell lines, iPSC-derived neurons, organoids), in vivo animal models, and in silico computational approaches. It argues that no single model captures the multifactorial complexity of these disorders, and that integrating experimental and computational strategies is needed to better dissect pathogenic mechanisms and support personalized therapeutic development.

papers.title: Digital Twins in Oncology: From Multimodal Data Integration to Precision Clinical Practice.
papers.abstract: Oncology digital twins are patient-specific computational models that are built by combining electronic health records, multiomics genomic data, and diagnostic imaging to simulate individual tumor biology and predict multiple treatment-related outcomes. Conceptually originated from aerospace engineering, it has matured clinically through convergent advances in radiomics, mechanistic tumor modeling, pharmacokinetic- pharmacodynamic systems, federated machine learning, and, most recently, large language model (LLM)-based clinical interfaces and agentic artificial intelligence (AI). For a practic
papers.journal: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging
papers.summary: This review describes oncology digital twins—patient-specific computational models that integrate electronic health records, multiomics data, and diagnostic imaging to simulate tumor biology and predict treatment outcomes. It traces the concept from aerospace engineering through advances in radiomics, mechanistic tumor modeling, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic systems, federated machine learning, and LLM-based clinical interfaces, framing these as convergent steps toward precision oncology practice.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis of extracellular vesicle cargo in cancer.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly recognized as minimally invasive sources of molecular information in cancer, carrying nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and metabolites that reflect tumor biology. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometry have not only enabled multi-omics profiling of EV cargo but also revealed that different molecular layers capture distinct yet complementary aspects of cancer processes. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the rapidly expanding landscape of EV multi-omics, highlighting methodological constraints, the predomin
papers.summary: This review surveys how extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry nucleic acids, proteins, lipids, and metabolites that reflect tumor biology, and how high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometry now enable multi-omics profiling of this cargo. It emphasizes that different molecular layers capture distinct yet complementary aspects of cancer processes, and discusses methodological constraints and the potential of EV multi-omics for minimally invasive cancer diagnostics.

papers.title: Implementing the ILAE 2025 seizure taxonomy in medical software.
papers.abstract: The International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE), working via a multidisciplinary task force, has issued a position paper with updated seizure classification guidelines (2025) replacing its previous guidance (2017), establishing a revised de-facto standard for clinical assessment and classification of epileptic seizures. The 2025 model simplifies the system, making it easier to adopt in different clinical settings while also clarifying the taxonomic rules, the definition of consciousness, and the application of phenomena-based descriptors. As a result, clinical practitioners, technologists, an
papers.summary: This paper describes how to implement the ILAE 2025 revised seizure classification taxonomy within medical software systems. The 2025 update simplifies the prior 2017 system, clarifies taxonomic rules and the definition of consciousness, and aims to make seizure classification more consistent across clinical settings. The authors translate these clinical guidelines into software-implementable logic.

papers.title: HuRInterDB: A Database Exploring the Landscape of lncRNA-Protein Interactions.
papers.abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) possess diverse biological functions and play key regulatory roles in biological processes by interacting with other biomolecules, such as proteins, RNAs, and the genome. High-throughput RNA-interaction experiments have generated large volumes of lncRNA-protein interaction records. The fragmented deposition of these records across disparate public databases complicates unified retrieval and integrative analysis. Here, we present HuRInterDB (Human lncRNA-Protein Interaction Database), a comprehensive and standardized database that focuses on human lncRNA-protein in
papers.summary: HuRInterDB is a new comprehensive database that consolidates human lncRNA-protein interaction data from disparate public sources into a standardized, unified resource. It aims to simplify retrieval and enable integrative analysis of these interactions, which are key to understanding lncRNA regulatory functions.

papers.title: ICD-11 and diabetes: opportunities for precision public health through enhanced classification.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus poses a major global health challenge, yet its intrinsic heterogeneity has been poorly captured by traditional classification systems. The international classification of diseases, tenth revision (ICD-10), built on a phenotype-based framework, lacks the granularity needed to incorporate contemporary molecular insights into diabetes subtypes, hampering both clinical precision and public health surveillance.
papers.summary: This paper argues that ICD-10's phenotype-based diabetes classification is too coarse to capture the disease's molecular heterogeneity, limiting both clinical precision and public health surveillance. It proposes that ICD-11's expanded classification offers opportunities to integrate contemporary molecular insights into diabetes subtypes, enabling more precise public health approaches.

papers.title: IMicAP: an intelligent microbial application platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms play a pivotal role in health and disease, yet microbial research is hindered by fragmented data, heterogeneous knowledge representation, and a lack of integrated analytical tools. Existing databases and knowledge graphs often focus narrowly on genomic information, leaving critical metabolomic and literature-based associations underdeveloped.
papers.summary: IMicAP is presented as an integrated platform for knowledge-driven microbiome research, aiming to address the fragmentation of microbial data and the narrow focus of existing databases on genomic information. The platform is designed to combine heterogeneous knowledge sources, including metabolomic and literature-based associations, into a unified analytical environment. The abstract describes the motivation and design rather than reporting specific findings or validation results.

papers.title: CfDNA methylation profiling in blood following moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury using brain cell type-enriched signatures: A pilot study.
papers.abstract: The human brain consists of diverse cell types that collaboratively perform complex functions and form intricate neuronal networks. When traumatic brain injury (TBI) occurs, multiple molecular pathways involving diverse cell types are activated in response to injury. Understanding how brain cell composition is altered during TBI may help improve patient outcomes. Upon brain trauma, neurovascular disruption leads to the release of brain-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA) into peripheral blood. The tissue-specific DNA methylation patterns in this cfDNA have the potential to serve as candidate markers
papers.summary: This pilot study profiled cell-free DNA methylation in blood from patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury, using methylation signatures enriched for specific brain cell types to infer changes in brain cell composition after trauma. The authors propose that tissue-specific methylation patterns in brain-derived cfDNA released into blood could serve as candidate biomarkers of injury. As a pilot, the work is exploratory and small-scale.

papers.title: Integrating cure and care in Alzheimer's disease: a systems perspective for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease remains a major global health challenge, with limited disease-modifying therapies and a rapidly growing societal burden. Although amyloid and tau remain central to the field, current evidence also implicates neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions in disease pathogenesis. These developments support a broader systems framework, but simply combining additional disciplines or data modalities does not by itself preserve the dynamic biology or lived experience of disease. Artificial intelligence multi-omics, and digital biomar
papers.summary: This perspective article argues that Alzheimer's disease research should move beyond amyloid and tau to a systems-level framework incorporating neuroinflammation, immune dysregulation, vascular dysfunction, and host-microbe interactions. The authors propose integrating AI, multi-omics, and digital biomarkers to support precision medicine that combines disease-modifying treatment with care, while cautioning that simply aggregating data modalities does not capture the dynamic biology or lived experience of disease.

papers.title: How AI-based techniques for brain tumour diagnosis can address data variability.
papers.abstract: Data variability in medical imaging of tumors refers to the inconsistencies in Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Computational Tomography scans caused by heterogeneous tumor biology, varying scanner hardware, and subjective human interpretation. This variability creates significant challenges for accurate diagnoses, treatment tracking, and AI model development. Although the variability in medical imaging data for diagnostic and prognostic purposes is a challenge for AI methods applied to other types of tumors as well, it is particularly problematic when the analysis involves gliomas and glioblast
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how data variability in brain tumour imaging—arising from heterogeneous tumour biology, differing scanner hardware, and subjective human interpretation—poses major challenges for AI-based diagnosis, especially for gliomas and glioblastomas. It outlines how AI techniques can be adapted to address this variability and improve diagnostic accuracy and treatment tracking.
